items.title: docs(id): talk-page semantics decision record (closes #5871)
items.body: Closes #5871. Decision record for talk-page semantics, settling the four questions #5682 §2 leaves open. Design only — no implementation code. **Decisions** 1. **Creation — lazy.** A talk page exists only as the `talk_for` binding on the first signed post; an undiscussed object costs zero storage and exposes no artifact. Clients may offer "start the discussion" to any object reader; nothing is pre-created. 2. **Permissions — intersection, narrowing-only.** `can_read(talk_page) = can_read(object) ∧ is_member(conversation)`. No override may widen past object read-authority. Cross-object threads intersect over *all* anchors. Hard rule: no content **or existence** leak — for a non-reader the page is indistinguishable from an object with no talk page. 3. **Lifecycle.** Archive makes posting fail at admission (architectural, not client-side); ownership transfer moves binding/governance authority with the object without re-binding; object tombstone **preserves** the conversation, folds the binding to `orphaned`, removes the object-side entry point, and never re-adopts the page on object re-creation; `talk_for` targeting a conversation is rejected so recursion is depth one. 4. **Moderation and binding — split.** Object owner governs structure (lock/close/pin/announce/slow) via signed events; server moderation (#835) retains takedown, implemented as signed events, never deletes. Only the object owner or an owner-named delegate may bind; unauthorized bindings are rejected at admission (disputed is for legitimate conflicts only). 5. **Mapping to existing code.** Membership is the object read set projected through group policy (`pkgs/id/src/groups/policy.rs`); `History::Full` for unconditional audiences, `History::FromJoin` when read-authority is granted per key, `Recent(n)` only to tighten. Revocation cannot un-deliver — stated as the design's one honest limitation, with key rotation left to #5801. **Explicitly recorded for parents/siblings:** #5682 §2 is preserved and only refined (the read-authority sentence is read as intersection + narrowing); #5872 is unchanged — this record supplies the binding authority and visibility intersection it delegated; #5870/#835/#5873/#5874/#5875 untouched. If #5682 intended "any object reader reads every thread regardless of membership", that is a parent change and is flagged rather than made silently. Nine testable invariants are in §6 (intersection at read time, no-existence-leak indistinguishability, narrowing-only as a property test, lazy equivalence, depth one, preservation, authority determinism, architectural archive, total history mapping). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: doc(id): decision record — thread resolution & the discussion→edit loop (#5874)
items.body: Decision record for #5874 (thread resolution and the discussion-to-edit loop), produced by queue task 13637 — the fix-family follow-on created by the task 10276 / task 12360 triages of #5874. Contents (doc-only, one file): chat.resolution.v1 and chat.proposal.v1 event kinds; resolution and proposal state as derived folds (never mutable fields), reusing the note_links pattern; acceptance = the accepting edit event citing the proposal; authorization and no-leak visibility rules from parent #5682; six implementation invariants; rejected alternatives; implementation split in section 8. Parent #5682 decisions, #5870 anchors, and #5871 talk-page semantics are explicitly not re-decided. Evidence baseline: origin/main 10da0c4ed2; verified no resolved-into/proposal mechanics exist in pkgs/ today, chat v1 ChatLinkKind is {Blob, Event}, and note_links carries the signed-link-event + derived-projection pattern this record extends. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: doc(id): terminal participation in object discussions — decision record (#5873)
items.body: Closes the design question on #5873 (follow-on of #5682, epic #2056). ## What this decides A decision record for **terminal participation in object discussions** — the third facet #5872 explicitly delegated ("Terminal rendering → #5873"). 1. **Terminal flows** — the terminal is a first-class participant, not a read-only mirror. The interface is the existing shared `world_line` grammar (already identical across SSH `cmd:`, the `id world join` pump and the CLI), extended with `/anchor`, `/talk`, `/anchors`, `/resolve`, `/queue`, `/flush`. No new TUI framework, no terminal-only protocol state. 2. **Textual anchor rendering** — anchors render as `[surface](id://)`, the form already settled by #2259, so a reference copied out of a terminal resolves in any other client. Disputed bindings and tombstoned anchors are always visible; unresolvable targets degrade without leaking existence. Part anchors render with a `#` fragment — **conditional on #5870**, which owns that grammar and has not landed. 3. **Offline compose** — sign at compose time, queue on the existing durable `Outbox`, replay on reconnect, never rewrite. Re-parenting, silent discard and signing at send time are all rejected by name. Also records 8 rejected alternatives with reasons, 11 testable invariants, and an explicit statement that **no parent decision changes**. ## Verification - Fresh `gh` checks: #5873, #5682, #5870, #5871, #5874, #5875, #2056 all OPEN; #5872 decision record confirmed landed and delegating terminal rendering here. - Every code claim checked against `origin/main` `0a27a7f19f`: `Outbox` (`enqueue`/`due`/`record`/`withdraw`/`entries`), the `world_line` verb set and its unknown-verb → `Message` behaviour, and the `id://` form in the #2259 spec. - Docs-only change; no code, no tests affected. ## Follow-on Implementation is a separate gated track (same gate #6222 carries): filed and linked from #5873. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
